title: Surge Scheduling Safeguard with Stochastic Targeting
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a new autoscaling policy component (Surge Scheduler) that uses stochastic demand targeting to smooth decisions across short bursts while enforcing hard safety fences (rate limits, cost budget, tenant caps). This ticket covers policy spec, scheduler implementation hooks, safety enforcement middleware, and integration tests for Dedicated fleets.
acceptance_criteria: New surge scheduler can accept target requests and emit scaling intents with a max increase of X nodes per minute configurable via fleet policy
Scheduler combines short-term stochastic throughput prediction with percentile latency targets (p95) to pick scale actions
Safety middleware prevents any scale action that violates per-tenant caps or global cost-envelope and records a decision audit event
E2E tests simulate bursts and validate latency SLOs remain within configured leeway while cost delta remains within budgeted tolerance
Documentation in the autoscaler policy guide and console rollout controls updated
proposed_design: We will add a Surge Scheduler module that consumes: recent throughput distribution (token/sec), inter-arrival tail statistics, p95/p99 latency estimates, and GPU occupancy. The scheduler runs a stochastic optimizer (lightweight sampling of demand scenarios over short horizon) to compute a robust target capacity that minimizes expected latency violation subject to cost budget and maximum slew constraints. Outputs are candidate scale intents which then pass through the Safety Enforcer component. Safety Enforcer applies deterministic fences (max nodes/minute, cooldown windows, tenant caps, reserved-headroom), logs decisions, and optionally rejects or downgrades intents to a graceful fallback (queueing, degrade-to-smaller-model).
scaling_algorithms: stochastic-targeting-sampler (primary): sample demand trajectories over next 30s-2m, choose capacity that keeps p95 latency < target under Xth percentile scenarios
derivative-limited-stepper: prevents large instantaneous deltas by applying slope limits to scale intents
predictive-warmup-hook: uses low-cost predictor to pre-warm KV cache affinities for upcoming replicas
pid-fallback: a legacy PID controller remains for environments without sampling telemetry
target_metrics: aggregate token throughput (tokens/sec) per tenant and fleet
request queue depth and queue wait-time percentiles
KV cache hit rate (for prefix-heavy workloads)
safety_limits: max_scale_rate: default 2 nodes/minute (configurable at fleet level)
burst_cooldown: 60s per-scale action unless overridden by manual policy
tenant_cap: per-tenant max nodes and committed headroom must not be exceeded
cost_envelope: monthly committed cost delta cannot be breached by autoscaler-triggered nodes without approval
min_stable_duration: new replicas must remain healthy for 90s before counted towards further scaling decisions
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime feature flag 'surge_scheduler_v1'. Start with dedicated internal test fleet (canary) for 24h, promote to low-traffic customer tier for 72h with aggressive telemetry. Monitor latency SLOs, cost, and decision audit logs. Default to disabled for fleets with existing custom autoscaler configs. Gradual rollout controlled from the Console 'Autoscale Rollouts' page.
test_plan: unit tests for scheduler sampling and optimizer boundary conditions
integration tests that inject synthetic burst traces and assert intent outputs
chaos test that flips off a subset of replicas to validate safe rollback and fallback
load soak on staging fleet for 48h with production-like request mix
dashboard smoke alerts: p95 increase > 10% post-deploy, unexpected cost delta > 8%
notes: Design trade-offs: sampling-based optimizer gives better tail protection at cost of CPU cycles; we limit samples and cache intermediate results to bound overhead
We opt for deterministic fences over advisory hints to simplify compliance and billing behavior
Fallbacks: if Safety Enforcer downgrades an intent, it will emit a telemetry tag to surface in the Console and to trigger SRE runbooks if repeated
